purpose: Measure whether re-confirmation of oracle NEGATIVES needs an operator. Every decision rule below is fixed before any data exists and does not change once the run starts.

the_gate_under_test.what_it_is: When the oracle returns a negative verdict on a lead — refuted, held, no-signal — that verdict is currently re-confirmed with operator attention before the lead is closed.
the_gate_under_test.why_this_one: docs/engineering/003-roadmap.md:98 names it 'the largest source of low-value operator attention'. Environment preflight is safer to graduate but runs once per engagement, so graduating it saves almost nothing and would be close to ceremonial.
the_gate_under_test.graduatable_at_all: Yes. engine/autonomy.md section 1 places information analysis at high autonomy by default. The two irreducible gates — Zone-2 confirmation and adjudicating `confirmed` — are NOT in scope here and are not affected by this measurement.

what_standby_means.changes: The gate still fires and still records. The run does NOT block waiting for the operator. Negatives are batched and only disagreements are surfaced.
what_standby_means.does_not_change: Nothing is removed. The operator watches and may override at any time. Restoring the gate costs a config change and a re-review of anything closed during the window.
what_standby_means.capture: Every time the operator would have overturned an automatic re-confirmation is recorded live: `tools/intervention_ledger.py live --engagement <id> ...` with `provenance: live`. Live entries are NEVER merged with backfilled ones into one statistic.

what_N_40_actually_licenses.operator_question: The operator asked whether N=40 is 'just for benchmarking'. Half true, and the half that is not matters.
what_N_40_actually_licenses.it_is_a_benchmark_in_that: It removes nothing, it is fully reversible, and running it costs only bookkeeping.
what_N_40_actually_licenses.it_is_NOT_just_a_benchmark_in_that: N=40 is the evidentiary basis that would license removing this gate. It is not a number we track; it is the sample a removal decision would rest on.
what_N_40_actually_licenses.the_bound: With N=40 and ZERO interventions, the rule of three puts the 95% upper bound on the true miss rate at 3/40 = 7.5%. That is NOT 'the gate is safe'. It is 'the miss rate is probably under 7.5%'. engine/autonomy.md section 5 requires this bound to be stated every single time the number is reported.
what_N_40_actually_licenses.is_7_5_percent_acceptable_here: Arguably yes for THIS gate, and the reasoning must be explicit rather than assumed. A miss means a lead was closed as negative when it was not. The lead is not a finding and nothing ships; downstream gates (G0-G6, regrade, pocinator) all still exist and all still run. The cost of a miss is a missed bug, not a false report to a vendor.
what_N_40_actually_licenses.where_7_5_percent_would_NOT_be_acceptabl: Decision selection (`confirmed`, severity) and action (Zone-2, filing). Those are the irreducible gates and this bound must never be used to argue about them.
what_N_40_actually_licenses.if_a_tighter_bound_is_wanted: N=100 with zero interventions gives ~3%. N=300 gives ~1%. The cost is engagement volume, not effort per engagement. Raising N later is legitimate; lowering it after seeing data is not.

metrics_fixed_before_data.M1_live_interventions: Count of operator overrides of an automatic negative re-confirmation, over N observed negatives. The headline number.
metrics_fixed_before_data.M2_intervention_class: Each override tagged with `judgement_class` from the existing enum. A cluster in `skepticism` means the gate catches over-closing; a cluster in `persistence` means it catches premature dry verdicts. Different clusters imply different fixes.
metrics_fixed_before_data.M3_reopened_negatives: Negatives closed during the window that a LATER round reopened on materially new construction. This is the only signal here that approaches ground truth, because it does not depend on anyone noticing at the time.
metrics_fixed_before_data.M4_batch_load: How many negatives per batch and how often. If the answer is 'few', the premise that this is the largest source of low-value attention is wrong and should be corrected rather than defended.
metrics_fixed_before_data.M5_latency_delta: Wall-clock from negative verdict to lead closure, standby versus the gated baseline. This is what graduation actually buys, and if it is small the graduation is not worth its risk.

decision_rule.graduate_if: M1 == 0 AND M3 == 0 across the full N=40, AND M5 shows a latency saving worth the residual risk. Report the 7.5% upper bound alongside the decision, always.
decision_rule.keep_the_gate_if: M1 >= 1 or M3 >= 1. Either means the gate is doing work, and that is a result worth having — it converts an assumption into a measurement.
decision_rule.inconclusive_if: Fewer than 40 negatives observed. Do not decide early. Do not lower N after seeing data.
decision_rule.no_partial_graduation: The gate is removed or it is not. A per-class breakdown is reported either way.

threats_to_validity: THE CENTRAL ONE: the quality proxy is operator override, which measures 'the operator disagreed', not 'the negative was wrong'. engine/autonomy.md section 4 requires a quality proxy WITH GROUND TRUTH, and this is weaker than that. A negative that was wrong and that nobody noticed is precisely the omission error Skitka measured as untrainable — it will not appear in M1. M3 (reopened negatives) is the partial mitigation and it is not sufficient on its own. This limitation must be restated in the outcome document, not buried.
An operator who knows a measurement is running may intervene more than they otherwise would, or less. This is not blinded and cannot be.

N=40 negatives may span several engagements and several target domains. Oracle validity does not transfer across namespaces (see the hulk-2026-07 phantom-route result), so a negative in one domain is not exchangeable with a negative in another. Report the per-engagement split.
The baseline for M5 does not exist yet. The first engagement in the window must record the gated latency before standby begins, or the saving cannot be computed.
The same author wrote the gate, this preregistration and the decision rule.

constraints_carried_from_doctrine.one_gate_at_a_time: engine/autonomy.md section 7. No other gate goes to standby while this runs. If quality drops, attribution must be unambiguous.
constraints_carried_from_doctrine.not_the_irreducible_two: Zone-2 confirmation and adjudicating `confirmed` are untouched and unaffected.
constraints_carried_from_doctrine.reversal: Restoring the gate is a config change plus a re-review of negatives closed during the window. Reversal must be rehearsed once before N is reached, not first attempted after a bad result.

recording.rule: The outcome document is written after the run and never edits this file. This file is the declared rule; the outcome is the decision against it.
